title: Navimower 0.4.4-beta17

## WGS84 ellipsoid geodesy reset

- Replace the local metre <-> latitude/longitude conversion used by georeference fitting and validation with WGS84 ellipsoid curvature instead of one fixed spherical Earth radius.
- Keep the existing local mower/map rigid transform model unchanged: local X/Y, map rotation, mowing geometry, dock geometry and live MQTT coordinates are not moved by this change.
- The change removes a latitude-dependent scale error that is small in Estonia but can reach roughly half a metre over a 100 m north/south span around Zimbabwe or Rio de Janeiro latitudes.
- Use the same ellipsoidal metre conversion for static vendor tie fitting, cloud XY/GPS fitting, reference diagnostics, X3 RTK comparisons and georeference validation through the shared Navimower helper functions.

## Stop automatic beta16 cartographic correction

- Do not automatically install the experimental beta16 ETRS89/ITRF cartographic-frame shift in production runtime.
- Keep the beta16 module and its direct regression tests available for research, but collect the next raw exports in the vendor geographic frame because Navimow does not declare the absolute CRS of its GNSS/map coordinates.
- This means H2/i1/i2 placement is no longer silently shifted by the Europe-only EPSG:8366 assumption while we compare fresh vendor/static/cloud evidence.

## X3

- Keep the existing X3 `RTK_anchor + nrtk_lrtk_bias` candidate active for this beta because the bias values are explicit vendor metadata with quality flags.
- Do not add any new X3 offset. Fresh raw data will be used to compare the vendor RTK candidate against the ellipsoid-correct cloud XY/GPS fit before deciding whether X3 should remain primary or become only a validation candidate.

## Field test / raw data

- After updating, let each available mower move across a reasonably wide part of its map before exporting fresh raw data so the cloud XY/GPS fit has useful spatial baseline.
- Collect new raw exports for H2, i1, i2 and X3 where possible. A docked snapshot is useful for local-frame checks, but a moving/wide-baseline snapshot is more important for georeference fitting.
- Do not judge the result only by visual orthophoto alignment yet. The next comparison should first separate local XY consistency, vendor geographic transform, cloud XY/GPS fit and any remaining cartographic-datum disagreement.
